title_en: Shanghai Meikuang Supply Chain Management Co., Ltd. and Pioneer Export Company v. Aodisaishi Shipping Trade Company, Haiwang Shipping Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over a maritime cargo transport contract
ruling_gist_en: Carriers, persons authorized to issue bills of lading, and other interested parties in the process of bill of lading issuance shall not rely solely on the statements of the interested parties as a basis for determining the authenticity of a bill of lading or distinguishing the priority of rights under bills of lading when two or more holders of original bills of lading each claim delivery of the same batch of goods carried by the carrier. Instead, the priority of rights under the bills of lading shall be comprehensively analyzed and determined based on the process of issuance of the bills of lading, the process by which the holders obtained the bills of lading, and in light of the international trade background and shipping practices.

full_text_en:
Shanghai Meikuang Supply Chain Management Co., Ltd. and Pioneer Export v. Audacious Shipping & Trading S.A., Kings Ocean Shipping Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over contract of carriage of goods by sea

【Ruling Summary】

The carrier, the person who issues bills of lading on behalf of the carrier, and other interested parties in the bill of lading issuance process are interested parties. When two or more holders of original bills of lading each claim delivery of the same cargo carried by the carrier, the statements of the interested parties alone cannot serve as the basis for identifying the authenticity of the bills of lading or distinguishing the priority of rights under the bills of lading. Instead, the superiority of rights under the bills of lading shall be determined based on a comprehensive analysis of the process of issuing the bills of lading, the process by which the holders came into possession of the bills of lading, and taking into account the international trade background and shipping practice.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2018) Supreme People's Court Min Zai No. 240

Retrial Applicant (Third Party at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shanghai Meikuang Supply Chain Management Co., Ltd. (formerly Shanghai Meikuang Mining Co., Ltd.). Domicile: Room 1185, Building 1, No. 333 Puhui Road, Jiading Industrial Zone, Shanghai, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Ma Wenying, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Yan Shengmin, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Feihang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Hu Xiaoli, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Huisheng Law Firm.

Retrial Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Pioneer Export. Domicile: Mahalaxmi Atta Mill Compound, Nirmal Nagar, Bhavnagar, Gujarat, 364001, Republic of India.

Representative: Pramil Khandelwal, Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wu Yimin, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Huarong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Yuesheng, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Lihe Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Audacious Shipping & Trading S.A. Domicile: Monrovia 80, Broad Street of the Republic of Liberia.

Representative: George Gourdomichalis, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Yang Liu, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Rongfu Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Kings Ocean Shipping Co., Ltd. Domicile: Sinmunnol (il)-ga, 20th Fl., S-Tower, Shinmunro1-ka, 82, Saemunan-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul, Korea.

Representative: Choi Dong Sun, Chairman of the Company.

Third Party at First Instance: Mineral Industrial Caspian Company. Domicile: No. 1 Aviz Alley, Alvand Street, Argentine Sq., Tehran, Iran.

Representative: Saeid Goudarzi, Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Tan Jie, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Feihang Law Firm.

In the case concerning the dispute over a contract of carriage of goods by sea between the retrial applicants Shanghai Meikuang Supply Chain Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Meikuang Company) and Pioneer Export (hereinafter referred to as Pioneer Company) and the respondents Audacious Shipping & Trading S.A. (hereinafter referred to as Audacious Company) and Kings Ocean Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kings Ocean Company), and the third party at first instance Mineral Industrial Caspian Company (hereinafter referred to as Mineral Company), the retrial applicants, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2016) Hu Min Zhong No. 119 rendered by the Shanghai High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of second instance), applied to this Court for retrial. On June 28, 2018, this Court rendered the civil ruling (2018) Supreme People's Court Min Shen No. 571, granting the retrial of this case. After granting the retrial, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing of this case on September 2, 2021. Yan Shengmin, agent ad litem of Meikuang Company, Wu Yimin and Zhao Yuesheng, agents ad litem of Pioneer Company, and Yang Liu, agent ad litem of Audacious Company, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. Mineral Company and Kings Ocean Company, having been served with summons by this Court, failed to appear in court without justifiable reasons. This case has been tried by default and is now concluded.

Pioneer Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting: 1. Compensation for cargo loss of RMB 17,251,124; 2. The two defendants to jointly and severally pay Pioneer Company interest loss, calculated on the principal of RMB 17,251,124 at the one-year bank deposit interest rate from April 14, 2014 to the date of actual enforcement; 3. The two defendants to bear the litigation costs. During the trial at first instance, Pioneer Company amended its claims to: 1. Compensation for cargo loss of RMB 17,251,124; 2. The two defendants to jointly and severally pay Pioneer Company interest loss, calculated on the principal of RMB 17,251,124 at the one-year bank deposit interest rate from April 14, 2014 to the date of entry of judgment; 3. The two defendants to bear the litigation costs; 4. An order that Pioneer Company is entitled to the proceeds from the sale of the cargo in dispute in the amount of RMB 6,821,281.95. Facts and reasons: The vessel "AUDACIOUS" loaded 45,475.213 metric tons of iron ore at an Iranian port on March 4, 2014. Kings Ocean Company's loading port agent, RAINBOW ATLAS OCEAN MARINE SERVICES LLC (hereinafter referred to as RAINBOW), signed bill of lading No. RM/BN/CH/011 on behalf of the vessel. Pioneer Company, as the shipper named on the bill of lading, obtained the full set of original bills of lading. The cargo arrived at Shanghai Port on April 12, 2014. Audacious Company, as the owner of the vessel, and Kings Ocean Company, as the charterer of the vessel for the relevant voyage, refused to deliver the cargo to Pioneer Company on the ground that a third party had raised an objection to the cargo. During this period, the international trading price of iron ore fell sharply, and the refusal of Audacious Company and Kings Ocean Company to deliver the cargo caused significant losses to Pioneer Company.

Meikuang Company submitted a "Motion to Add Third Party" to the court of first instance, requesting an order that Audacious Company and Kings Ocean Company jointly deliver the cargo in dispute to it, or if unable to deliver the cargo, compensate for the cargo value loss of RMB 6,821,281.95, the loss in market value of the cargo due to the failure to release the cargo in a timely manner of RMB 9,100,345.25, and interest. Facts and reasons: Mineral Company was the owner of the cargo under the bill of lading and the actual shipper/delivery shipper, and obtained the full set of original bills of lading after the cargo was loaded. As Mineral Company owed Meikuang Company monies, Mineral Company had offset the cargo under the aforesaid bill of lading to Meikuang Company and delivered the full set of original bills of lading to Meikuang Company. Meikuang Company, as the lawful holder of the full set of bills of lading, had a lawful basis and right to demand that Audacious Company and Kings Ocean Company deliver the cargo under the bill of lading to it.

The court of first instance found the following facts:

On February 5, 2014, Mineral Company entered into a sales contract with SACVINAM GLOBAL LIMITED (hereinafter referred to as SGL), agreeing that Mineral Company would sell iron ore fines to SGL, quantity 50,000 wet metric tons, +10% at buyer's option, country of origin Iran, producer SABANOOR MINES, cargo price USD 59.75 per dry metric ton. On February 19, 2014, the parties entered into a supplemental agreement, amending the quantity to 45,500 wet metric tons.

On February 6, 2014, Pioneer Company entered into a sales contract with CBH CORPORATION LIMITED (hereinafter referred to as CBH), agreeing that CBH would sell iron ore fines to Pioneer Company, quantity 50,000 wet metric tons, +10% at buyer's option, country of origin Iran, producer SABA NOOR MINES, cargo price USD 59.75 per dry metric ton.

Audacious Company was the owner of the vessel "AUDACIOUS". On November 5, 2013, Audacious Company and Kings Ocean Company entered into a time charter party, agreeing that Audacious Company would time charter the "AUDACIOUS" to Kings Ocean Company for a period of 3-5 months, at the charterer's option, with the crew provided by the owner Audacious Company. The time charter party also provided that the owner authorized the charterer or its agents to sign bills of lading on behalf of the master or the owner in accordance with the mate's receipts. Kings Ocean Company confirmed in court that during the carriage of the cargo in dispute, it remained the time charterer of the "AUDACIOUS". On February 10, 2014, Kings Ocean Company entered into a voyage charter party with RADIANT INTERNATIONAL FZC (hereinafter referred to as RADIANT), agreeing that RADIANT would charter the "AUDACIOUS" to transport the cargo in dispute. On March 4, 2014, a mate's receipt was issued for the "AUDACIOUS", stating the shipper as Mineral Company. On the same day, the master of the "AUDACIOUS", David Bolkvadze, issued a letter of authorization to RAINBOW on behalf of the "AUDACIOUS", authorizing RAINBOW to issue original bills of lading on behalf of the master for the relevant voyage.

Pursuant to the sales contract, Pioneer Company paid a 50% down payment to CBH and obtained a full set of bills of lading numbered RM/BN/CH/011. The bill of lading stated: shipper Pioneer Company, consignee and notify party to order, port of loading Persian Gulf Port, port of discharge any major port in China, carrying vessel "AUDACIOUS", cargo iron ore fines, quantity 45,475.213 wet metric tons. The bill of lading was signed by RAINBOW on March 4, 2014, on behalf of the master of the "AUDACIOUS". Pioneer Company stated in court that the bill of lading it held was collected by an employee of RADIANT directly from RAINBOW's office in Iran.

SGL paid Mineral Company a total of 50% of the trade contract price, USD 1,359,312.50, in two installments on February 28, 2014 and March 12, 2014. Mineral Company confirmed receipt of the 50% payment and issued an invoice to SGL.

Mineral Company obtained a full set of bills of lading also numbered RM/BN/CH/011. The contents recorded on the bill of lading were consistent with those on the bill of lading held by Pioneer Company, but there were minor differences in certain printed font and seals.

On April 23, 2014, FOOLAD SABANOOR PRIMARY MATERIALS COMPANY (hereinafter referred to as SABA) sent a letter stating that the cargo in dispute was sold by it to Mineral Company, and the cargo under bill of lading No. RM/BN/CH/011 had been transferred to Mineral Company. On the same day, Lelia, a former employee of RADIANT, issued a statement claiming that she was previously an employee of RADIANT or SGL or ROYALLINE RESOURCES LTD or ROSHAN PARTO QUESHM, and on April 12, 2014, she delivered all original documents including the original bills of lading to Mineral Company, and she did not send an email on April 14, 2014, claiming to still hold the aforesaid original documents.

On April 12, 2014, the cargo arrived at Shanghai Port. On June 3, 2014, after Pioneer Company's oral request for delivery was refused, it applied to the court of first instance for a seizure of the cargo. On the same day, the court of first instance rendered the civil ruling (2014) Hu Hai Fa Hai Bao Zi No. 38, granting Pioneer Company's application and seizing the cargo of 45,475.213 metric tons of iron ore at the Luojing Branch of Shanghai Port Group.

On June 4, 2014, Pioneer Company, holding the bill of lading, requested delivery from Shanghai Huagang International Ship Agency Co., Ltd., the Shanghai port agent of Kings Ocean Company, but was refused. On June 5, 2014, RAINBOW sent a letter to Kings Ocean Company, confirming that the bill of lading held by Pioneer Company was not an original bill of lading issued by it, and the seal was forged.

On June 4, 2014, Meikuang Company submitted a written arbitration application to the Shanghai Sub-Commission of the China Maritime Arbitration Commission (hereinafter referred to as the CMAC Shanghai Sub-Commission), requesting Mineral Company to repay USD 5,000,000, interest, attorney's fees, and other arbitration claims. On June 7, 2014, Mineral Company and Meikuang Company reached a settlement agreement. On June 30, 2014, the CMAC Shanghai Sub-Commission issued the award (2014) Hai Zhong Hu Cai Zi No. 049, awarding that Mineral Company deliver the bill of lading in dispute and another bill of lading numbered RM/BN/CH/012 to Meikuang Company, so that Meikuang Company could take delivery of the cargo from the carrier, to offset the outstanding payment of USD 5,000,000 and interest. On September 24, 2014, the CMAC Shanghai Sub-Commission sent a letter to the court of first instance, stating: "In this case, the arbitral tribunal did not make a determination on the ownership of the cargo. It only determined, based on the relevant evidence and the fact that the respondent actually held the relevant bills of lading, that the respondent had a prima facie right to take delivery of the cargo. ... The conflict that the applicant's right to take delivery of the cargo confirmed by the arbitration award might have with other prima facie rights to take delivery of the cargo is not within the scope of the arbitral tribunal's review in this case. ... As to whether the relevant facts involved in the arbitration award can be used as evidence, it is up to your court to decide after substantive trial."

During the trial of this case, the international iron ore price dropped significantly and continuously. All parties filed applications with the court of first instance to sell the cargo in dispute on grounds such as reducing losses, fixing the cargo value, and reducing storage costs. On December 23, 2014, after bidding, Pioneer Company purchased the cargo in dispute at a price of RMB 6,821,281.95. To take delivery of the cargo, Pioneer Company also paid import customs delay penalty of RMB 20,110 and storage fees of RMB 500,000.

The court of first instance held:

This case is a dispute over a contract of carriage of goods by sea. Pioneer Company, Audacious Company, Kings Ocean Company, and Mineral Company are all enterprises registered outside China, and the port of loading for the carriage in dispute is outside China. Therefore, this case involves foreign elements. Regarding the applicable law for this case, all parties claimed that Chinese law should apply. The court of first instance held that, under Chinese law, parties to a foreign-related contract may agree on the governing law for resolving the contract dispute. Therefore, the court of first instance determined that the laws of the People's Republic of China shall be the governing law for adjudicating this dispute.

Pursuant to Article 71 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, a bill of lading is a document which serves as evidence of the contract of carriage of goods by sea and the taking over or loading of the goods by the carrier, and based on which the carrier undertakes to deliver the goods against surrender of the document. It can be said that the bill of lading represents the goods. According to the principle of "one thing, one right" in property law, there shall be only one set of original bills of lading as the document representing the rights to the goods. In this case, both Pioneer Company and Meikuang Company each held a set of bills of lading for the cargo in dispute. Therefore, identifying the authenticity of the two sets of bills of lading is the key to resolving the dispute. However, before distinguishing the authenticity of the bills of lading, a premise should be clarified: the basis of review in this case should be established on the dispute over the contract of carriage of goods by sea, i.e., which of Pioneer Company and Meikuang Company can enjoy the right to take delivery of the cargo by virtue of holding the original bills of lading. The review may involve issues such as the payment of consideration for the bills of lading, but the basis of review is definitely not established on a trade contract, nor is it to review which of Pioneer Company and Meikuang Company owns the cargo in dispute. This case is a dispute over a contract of carriage of goods by sea. Both Pioneer Company and Meikuang Company have made claims against the carrier, requesting the carrier to deliver the cargo or the equivalent value of the cargo, and to compensate for losses caused by the refusal to deliver the cargo. This case is not a trade contract dispute, and neither Pioneer Company nor Meikuang Company has made a claim against the other for confirmation of ownership. Although both Pioneer Company and Meikuang Company submitted their respective trade contracts, the trade contracts are not connected to each other, the trade chain is incomplete, and trade disputes are not within the scope of review in a dispute over a contract of carriage of goods by sea. Therefore, the court of first instance will not make any determination on the relevant facts of trade circulation in this case. If Pioneer Company and Meikuang Company have any claims based on trade, they shall file a separate trade lawsuit to resolve them.

1. Distinguishing the Authenticity of the Two Sets of Original Bills of Lading.
Xianfeng Company and Meikuang Company each hold one set of original bills of lading. The contents of the bills of lading are identical in all respects, with the only differences being minor variations in some printed fonts and seals. Based on the evidence presented by the parties in this case, it is impossible to infer from the existing evidence alone who participated in the counterfeiting of the bills of lading. However, in terms of the surface form and content of the two sets of bills of lading involved, the two bills of lading are almost identical and could be easily mistaken for genuine ones. The question is which set of bills of lading was actually issued by the carrier to the shipper and can serve as a valid document representing the goods in question.
(1) Who has the authority to determine the authenticity of the bills of lading.
First, a bill of lading shall be signed by the carrier, the master, or an agent authorized by them. In this case, the bill of lading was signed by the signing agent Rainbow Company on behalf of the master. As the issuer, Rainbow Company is significantly more capable than other parties of identifying bills of lading it has issued. The existing evidence in this case shows that Rainbow Company confirmed that the bill of lading held by Minerals Company is genuine and valid, while the bill of lading held by Xianfeng Company is counterfeit.
Second, regardless of whether the bill of lading is issued by the master or the signing agent, the party bearing the rights and obligations arising from the bill of lading is always the carrier. The carrier controls the format and issuance of the bill of lading and is also responsible for verifying the authenticity of the bill of lading and for properly managing and delivering the goods while they are in its custody. Therefore, the carrier's identification of the bill of lading should also serve as one basis for distinguishing the authenticity of the bill of lading. In this case, both Odyssey Company and Neptune Company agreed with Rainbow Company's opinion, determining that the bill of lading held by Xianfeng Company is counterfeit.
(2) Issuance of the bill of lading.
The issuance of a bill of lading refers to the act of preparing the bill of lading and delivering it to the shipper or its agent, consisting of three actions: preparation, signing, and delivery. Among these, the delivery of the bill of lading, or the manner in which Xianfeng Company and Meikuang Company obtained the bills of lading, is a critical point of review in this case. In this case, Minerals Company stated that after Rainbow Company issued the bill of lading, it was delivered to Lelia, and Minerals Company exchanged the mate's receipt for the bill of lading from Lelia. This statement was confirmed by Lelia, Odyssey Company, and Neptune Company. In contrast, Xianfeng Company stated that its bill of lading was obtained by an employee of Radiant Company from Rainbow Company's premises. Xianfeng Company's statement was not confirmed by Odyssey Company or Neptune Company, and Xianfeng Company did not further provide evidence to support its assertion. According to the law, a party has the responsibility to provide evidence for the claims it makes. Xianfeng Company's self-described method of obtaining the bill of lading was not supported by any evidence, meaning Xianfeng Company could not prove that its bill of lading was obtained through proper channels, nor could it explain the true circumstances of the issuance process of the order bill of lading it held. Therefore, the legality of the source from which Xianfeng Company obtained the bill of lading could not be confirmed by the court of first instance.
(3) Payment of consideration for the bill of lading.
Whether the holder of a bill of lading has paid consideration in the trade contract is generally not a factor to be considered in the performance of a contract of carriage of goods by sea. The carrier is obligated to deliver the goods upon presentation of the bill of lading by the holder, without the need to review the trade flow process. However, in the special circumstances of this case, where two sets of original bills of lading exist for the same goods, whether consideration was paid to obtain the bill of lading becomes one of the factors to be considered in determining the authenticity of the bill of lading. In this case, both Xianfeng Company and Minerals Company confirmed that Xianfeng Company had paid 50% of the purchase price to its seller, CBH Company. However, according to the terms of the trade contract, the ownership of the goods would only transfer to Xianfeng Company after payment of 98% of the purchase price. Furthermore, Xianfeng Company stated that it did not obtain the bill of lading from its seller, CBH Company, but directly from the signing agent Rainbow Company. Therefore, this case does not involve obtaining the bill of lading after payment of consideration.
In summary, Odyssey Company, Neptune Company, and the signing agent Rainbow Company all denied the authenticity of the bill of lading held by Xianfeng Company. Xianfeng Company failed to provide evidence that it obtained the bill of lading through lawful and valid channels and paid the 98% of the purchase price as stipulated in the trade contract. Consequently, the bill of lading held by Xianfeng Company is not a valid document of title representing the goods in question. The bill of lading held by Meikuang Company was confirmed as genuine and valid by Odyssey Company, Neptune Company, and the signing agent, and the method by which it obtained the bill of lading was also confirmed by Odyssey Company, Neptune Company, and Rainbow Company. Therefore, the court of first instance confirmed the authenticity of the bill of lading it holds.

2. Legal Status of Odyssey Company and Neptune Company.
That is, on whose behalf did Rainbow Company issue the bill of lading, and who is the carrier in the contract of carriage of goods by sea in this case.
(1) The relationship between Odyssey Company and Neptune Company is a time charter party contract. Odyssey Company, as the shipowner, time-chartered the vessel "AUDACIOUS" to Neptune Company for use. During the period of the carriage of goods by sea in this case, Neptune Company remained the time charterer of the "AUDACIOUS".
(2) Odyssey Company and Neptune Company did not themselves issue the bill of lading, nor did they directly authorize any signing agent to issue the bill of lading in question. According to Article 72 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, "After the carrier receives the goods for carriage or loads them on board, the carrier shall, upon the request of the shipper, issue a bill of lading. The bill of lading may be issued by a person authorized by the carrier. Where a bill of lading is issued by the master of the ship carrying the goods, it shall be deemed to have been issued on behalf of the carrier." It can be seen that the issuers of a bill of lading include the carrier, an agent of the carrier, and the master. According to the power of attorney for issuing bills of lading submitted by Odyssey Company as evidence, for the voyage in question, the master authorized Rainbow Company to issue the bill of lading. The bill of lading in this case also shows that Rainbow Company issued the bill of lading on behalf of the master.
(3) Did the master represent the shipowner or the charterer? According to the terms of the time charter party contract entered into between Odyssey Company and Neptune Company, the shipowner, Odyssey Company, was responsible for providing the master and crew and for the navigation and internal management of the vessel. Therefore, unless Odyssey Company had expressly stated otherwise beforehand, the bill of lading issued by the master shall be deemed to have been issued on behalf of Odyssey Company. Even though Odyssey Company has consistently claimed that its authorization to Rainbow Company was limited to issuing bills of lading based on the mate's receipt, this is an internal agreement between Odyssey Company and Rainbow Company and is unrelated to the shipper recorded on the bill of lading issued externally.
In summary, Odyssey Company is the carrier in the contract of carriage of goods by sea in this case and shall bear the carrier's responsibility to the shipper in accordance with the contents of the bill of lading.

3. Whether Meikuang Company Obtained the Bill of Lading Originally Held by Minerals Company by Virtue of the Arbitration Award.
When Meikuang Company filed its application for arbitration with the Shanghai Sub-Commission of the China Maritime Arbitration Commission, the goods in question had already been sealed up by the court of first instance due to the dispute arising from the existence of two sets of bills of lading. Although Minerals Company knew that the goods in question had been seized by the court and that its right to take delivery of the goods under its bill of lading was in doubt, and that a court judgment was needed to clarify whether a bill of lading right existed, it still used the goods in question to offset its debts and reached a settlement agreement with Meikuang Company. Such an act constitutes unauthorized disposition. Therefore, Meikuang Company cannot acquire the right to take delivery of the goods in question against the bill of lading based on the settlement agreement or the arbitration award. Minerals Company should first ensure that it has the right to dispose of the goods in question before using the bill of lading as a valid document of title representing the goods to offset its debts.
In summary, Meikuang Company did not acquire the rights to the goods recorded in the bill of lading originally held by Minerals Company, and such bill of lading rights remain with Minerals Company.

4. Whether It Is Possible to Demand Delivery of Goods from the Carrier Using the Bill of Lading in Hand That Has Been Confirmed as Genuine and Valid.
An order bill of lading is a bill of lading in which the column for the consignee contains the words "to the order of" or "bearer". It can be further divided into named order and bearer order bills of lading. In this case, the bill of lading held by Meikuang Company is a bearer order bill of lading. This type of bill of lading shall be deemed to be subject to the order of the shipper, meaning that the bill of lading is transferred and the goods delivered by way of endorsement according to the instructions of the shipper recorded on the bill of lading. Therefore, although the bill of lading held by Meikuang Company is genuine, it must be endorsed by the shipper recorded on the bill of lading, Xianfeng Company, before Meikuang Company can demand delivery of the goods from the carrier against it. Otherwise, the chain of endorsement is incomplete, and it still cannot demand delivery of the goods from the carrier against this bill of lading.

In summary, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment:
(1) Reject all claims of Xianfeng Company.
(2) Reject all claims of Meikuang Company.
The case acceptance fee is RMB 162,162, to be borne by Xianfeng Company. The case acceptance fee for the third party is RMB 117,330, reduced by half to RMB 58,665, to be borne by Meikuang Company.

Both Xianfeng Company and Meikuang Company, being dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the court of second instance.

Xianfeng Company's grounds of appeal: The key issues in this case are who is the right holder under the bill of lading in question and whether the release of the bill of lading held by Minerals Company by Odyssey Company and Neptune Company was lawful. The court of first instance did not adjudicate the disputed issues raised by the parties, making it impossible for Xianfeng Company to achieve the purpose of its lawsuit. Minerals Company sold FOB goods and was not involved in the transportation matters, nor was it a party recorded on the bill of lading; therefore, it had no right to obtain the bill of lading in question. Meikuang Company also has no right to any rights under the bill of lading in question. Xianfeng Company's claims are legally well-founded. Accordingly, Xianfeng Company requests the court of second instance to reverse the judgment according to law and support all claims of Xianfeng Company in the first instance.

Meikuang Company's grounds of appeal: Minerals Company's act of offsetting debts with goods is lawful and valid, so Meikuang Company also lawfully obtained the bill of lading. The relationship between Meikuang Company and Minerals Company is not a transfer of the bill of lading under a trade contract, but rather an assignment of creditor's rights based on the offset of debts, through which Meikuang Company obtained the exact same rights as the assignor, Minerals Company, under the bill of lading. Accordingly, Meikuang Company requests the court of second instance to reverse the judgment according to law and support all claims of Meikuang Company in the first instance.

Odyssey Company argued in defense: This case is a dispute over the right to take delivery of goods arising from a bill of lading. The scope of review should be limited to whether the carrier should deliver the goods and whether the carrier was at fault for not delivering the goods. The ownership of the goods is not within the scope of review of this case. Xianfeng Company holds a counterfeit bill of lading. A prudent carrier needs to release the goods only against the presentation of the bill of lading. Since Xianfeng Company has not obtained the original bill of lading, it has no right to demand that Odyssey Company bear the fault for failure to deliver the goods.

Meikuang Company, in substance, obtained the bill of lading by reaching a settlement agreement with Minerals Company and then through arbitration. The bill of lading itself was not continuously endorsed, so the carrier's refusal to deliver the goods against the bill of lading is entirely reasonable. For Meikuang Company to claim that it lawfully obtained the bill of lading through an assignment of creditor's rights, it must first prove that Minerals Company's bill of lading was lawfully and validly obtained. However, the bill of lading was not endorsed to Minerals Company, so Odyssey Company could not determine whether Minerals Company lawfully held the bill of lading. The rights acquired by Meikuang Company based on this are also flawed. The original judgment was reasonable. Accordingly, Odyssey Company requests the court of second instance to dismiss the appeals and uphold the original judgment.

Neptune Company and Minerals Company did not submit written opinions.

During the second instance proceedings, the parties submitted evidence in support of their respective appeals in accordance with the law. The court of second instance organized the parties for exchange of evidence and cross-examination. Meikuang Company submitted the following evidentiary material: a printout of an email sent by Minerals Company to Odyssey Company and Neptune Company instructing the shipowner and Neptune Company to deliver the goods under the bill of lading to Meikuang Company, to prove that Meikuang Company holds three original bills of lading.

Xianfeng Company argued in cross-examination: (1) The authenticity of this evidentiary material cannot be determined, and its truthfulness is not recognized. (2) Minerals Company is not the shipper in this case, so its instructions are invalid. (3) The transfer of the bill of lading, which Minerals Company obtained illegally, to Meikuang Company constitutes fraud.

Odyssey Company argued in cross-examination: It does not recognize the truthfulness, legality, or relevance of this evidentiary material.

The court of second instance, unable to confirm the truthfulness of the evidentiary material as it was a printout of an email, declined to admit this evidentiary material.

No other parties submitted new evidentiary materials.

The court of second instance confirmed the other facts found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance additionally found: Shanghai Meikuang Mining Co., Ltd. is now renamed as Shanghai Meikuang Supply Chain Management Co., Ltd.

The court of second instance held that, according to Article 71 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, a bill of lading is a document which serves as evidence of the contract of carriage of goods by sea and the taking over or loading of the goods by the carrier, and based on which the carrier undertakes to deliver the goods against its production. According to the principle of one right for one thing in property law, there shall be one and only one set of original bills of lading as documents representing the goods.

Regarding the distinction between the authenticity of the two sets of bills of lading. First, a bill of lading shall be issued by the carrier, the master, or an agent authorized by them. In this case, the bill of lading was issued by the signing agent Rainbow Company on behalf of the master. As the issuer, Rainbow Company is significantly more capable than any other party of identifying bills of lading it has issued. The existing evidence in this case shows that Rainbow Company confirmed that the bill of lading held by Minerals Company is genuine and valid, while the bill of lading held by Xianfeng Company is counterfeit. Second, regardless of whether the bill of lading is issued by the master or the signing agent, the party bearing the rights and obligations arising from the bill of lading is always the carrier. The carrier controls the format and issuance of the bill of lading and is also responsible for verifying the authenticity of the bill of lading and for properly managing and delivering the goods while they are in its custody. Therefore, the carrier's identification of the bill of lading should also serve as one basis for distinguishing the authenticity of the bill of lading. In this case, both Odyssey Company and Neptune Company agreed with Rainbow Company's opinion, determining that the bill of lading held by Xianfeng Company is counterfeit. Third, the method of obtaining the bill of lading is a critical point of review in this case. In this case, Minerals Company stated that after Rainbow Company issued the bill of lading, it was delivered to Lelia, and Minerals Company exchanged the mate's receipt for the bill of lading from Lelia. This statement was confirmed by Lelia, Odyssey Company, and Neptune Company. In contrast, Xianfeng Company stated that its bill of lading was obtained by an employee of Radiant Company from Rainbow Company's premises. Xianfeng Company's statement was not confirmed by Odyssey Company or Neptune Company, and Xianfeng Company did not further provide evidence to support its assertion. According to the law, a party has the responsibility to provide evidence for the claims it makes. Xianfeng Company's self-described method of obtaining the bill of lading was not supported by any evidence, meaning Xianfeng Company could not prove that its bill of lading was obtained through proper channels, nor could it explain the true circumstances of the issuance process of the order bill of lading it held. Therefore, the legality of the source from which Xianfeng Company obtained the bill of lading cannot be confirmed. Fourth, whether the holder of the bill of lading paid consideration in the trade contract. In the special circumstances of this case, where two sets of bills of lading exist for the same goods, whether consideration was paid to obtain the bill of lading becomes one of the factors to be considered in determining the authenticity of the bill of lading. In this case, both Xianfeng Company and Minerals Company confirmed that Xianfeng Company had paid 50% of the purchase price to its seller, CBH Company. However, according to the terms of the trade contract, the ownership of the goods would only transfer to Xianfeng Company after payment of 98% of the purchase price. Furthermore, Xianfeng Company stated that it did not obtain the bill of lading from its seller, CBH Company, but directly from the signing agent Rainbow Company. Therefore, this case does not involve obtaining the bill of lading after payment of consideration.
In summary, Odyssey Company, Neptune Company, and the signing agent Rainbow Company all denied the authenticity of the bill of lading held by Xianfeng Company. Xianfeng Company failed to provide evidence that it obtained the bill of lading through lawful and valid channels and paid the 98% of the purchase price as stipulated in the trade contract. Consequently, the bill of lading held by Xianfeng Company is not a valid document of title representing the goods in question.

Regarding whether Meikuang Company obtained the bill of lading originally held by Minerals Company by virtue of the arbitration award. When Meikuang Company filed its application for arbitration with the Shanghai Sub-Commission of the China Maritime Arbitration Commission, the goods in question had already been sealed up by the court of first instance due to the dispute arising from the existence of two sets of bills of lading. Although Minerals Company knew that the goods in question had been seized by the court and that its right to take delivery of the goods under its bill of lading was in doubt, and that a court judgment was needed to clarify whether a bill of lading right existed, it still used the goods in question to offset its debts and reached a settlement agreement with Meikuang Company. Such an act constitutes unauthorized disposition. Therefore, Meikuang Company cannot acquire the right to take delivery of the goods in question against the bill of lading based on the settlement agreement or the arbitration award.

In this case, the bill of lading held by Meikuang Company is a bearer order bill of lading. This type of bill of lading shall be deemed to be subject to the order of the shipper, meaning that the bill of lading is transferred and the goods delivered by way of endorsement according to the instructions of the shipper recorded on the bill of lading. Therefore, the bill of lading held by Meikuang Company must be endorsed by the shipper recorded on the bill of lading, Xianfeng Company, before Meikuang Company can demand delivery of the goods from the carrier against it. Otherwise, the chain of endorsement is incomplete, and it still cannot demand delivery of the goods from the carrier against this bill of lading.

In summary, the bill of lading held by Xianfeng Company is counterfeit; the bill of lading held by Meikuang Company was not validly and continuously endorsed, so it has no right to the rights to the goods recorded on the bill of lading. The court of second instance rendered the following judgment: Dismiss the appeals and uphold the original judgment.

Meikuang Company applied to this Court for retrial of this case, requesting that the judgments of first and second instance be vacated and that all claims of Meikuang Company be supported, and that Odyssey Company, Neptune Company, and Xianfeng Company bear all litigation costs. The main facts and reasons are: (1) The basic facts determined by the judgment of second instance lack evidence. Meikuang Company's basis for demanding delivery of goods from the carrier is the debt offset agreement confirmed by the award of the Shanghai Sub-Commission of the China Maritime Arbitration Commission, not the bill of lading. During the second instance proceedings, Meikuang Company provided an email from Minerals Company titled "Release Instruction", which was obtained through notarization. The judgment of second instance ignored the notarial deed and wrongly refused to recognize its authenticity on the ground that the material was a printout of an email. (2) The judgment of second instance applied the law incorrectly. a. The determination that Minerals Company's act of offsetting debts with goods constituted an unauthorized disposition was wrong. As the actual shipper, Minerals Company had the right to obtain the full set of original bills of lading from the carrier. Its act of delivering the bill of lading pursuant to the creditor's rights assignment agreement does not constitute a transfer of the bill of lading and does not require endorsement, nor is it possible to endorse it. As a lawful holder of the bill of lading, Minerals Company's rights to the goods in question are not lost by reason of the court's seizure. b. It was wrong to directly deny the legal effect of the arbitration award. Meikuang Company has the right to take delivery of the goods from the carrier or to obtain the proceeds of sale based on the effective arbitration award. c. While the judgment of second instance determined that the bill of lading held by Xianfeng Company is false and that Xianfeng Company has no right to take delivery of the goods, it simultaneously deprived Meikuang Company of its right to take delivery of the goods on the ground that the bill of lading held by Meikuang Company is genuine but the chain of endorsement is incomplete, thereby rendering the goods in question ownerless. The judgment of second instance forcibly determined that the rights to the goods in question belong to Minerals Company, which violates the principle of "no trial without complaint".

Xianfeng Defense: (1) Meikuang admitted that "in this case, it relied on the creditor's rights assignment agreement rather than the bill of lading to take delivery of the goods," which violates legal provisions and international shipping practices. 1. The Reply Letter No. (2014) Haizhong Hu Zi 589 issued by the arbitral tribunal stated that the arbitral tribunal did not make a judgment on the ownership of the goods and had explained to the parties during the proceedings the commercial risks of transferring the right to take delivery under the bill of lading. Under these circumstances, Meikuang still reached a settlement agreement, which constitutes obvious fault. In its Application for Retrial, Meikuang admitted that it relied on the creditor's rights assignment agreement rather than the bill of lading to take delivery of the goods in question. Since this case is a dispute over a contract of carriage of goods by sea, Meikuang's claim should not be upheld. (2) The new evidence submitted by Meikuang, the "Delivery Order," does not meet the formal requirements and prerequisites for recognizing delivery and has no legal effect. Moreover, Neptune Company stated in the "Interview Record" dated December 23, 2014, that "the order we confirmed for lifting the goods is different from the bill of lading held by the plaintiff and Meikuang." (3) This case is a dispute over a contract of carriage of goods by sea. Neither Meikuang nor its upstream Mineral Company is a party to the contract of carriage of goods by sea or the lawful holder of the bill of lading in question, and they have no right to claim delivery of the goods. In summary, the request is to dismiss Meikuang's retrial application.

Xianfeng also applied to this Court for a retrial, requesting the revocation of the first instance judgment's first item and the judgment on the case acceptance fee; the revocation of the second instance judgment; and the amendment of the judgment to support all of Xianfeng's claims. Main facts and reasons: (1) The original trial court had procedural defects. Without conducting a judicial appraisal of the signatures and seals on the two sets of bills of lading, the original trial court determined that the bill of lading held by Xianfeng was forged solely based on the unilateral statement of the bill of lading issuer, lacking factual basis. (2) The original trial court erred in fact-finding and application of law. The bill of lading in question lists the shipper as Xianfeng. According to the relevant provisions of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China and the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the carrier should deliver the goods according to the instructions of the shipper. The trade term in this case is FOB, with the buyer responsible for chartering and booking shipping space and paying freight, insurance premiums, etc. The four new pieces of evidence submitted by Xianfeng, including the chartering declaration issued by RADIANT Company and the purchase of insurance declaration issued by Sacvianam, can prove that Xianfeng was responsible for chartering, booking shipping space, purchasing insurance, and paying the corresponding costs. As the holder of the bill of lading, Xianfeng has the right to claim delivery of the goods from the carrier. Odysseas Company and Neptune Company, by refusing to deliver the goods on the grounds that the bill of lading was forged, should bear the corresponding liability for damages.

Odysseas Company's defense against the retrial applications of Meikuang and Xianfeng: The first and second instance judgments correctly found the facts and applied the law. The request is to dismiss the retrial applications of Meikuang and Xianfeng. (1) The bill of lading held by Xianfeng is forged, and Odysseas Company's refusal to deliver the goods has a legal basis. Although the original trial court did not conduct an appraisal of the seal on the bill of lading held by Xianfeng, based on the explanations provided by RAINBOW Company, the letter from Leila, and the correspondence between Neptune Company, Mineral Company, etc., it can be proven that the bill of lading held by Xianfeng is forged. The new evidence submitted by Xianfeng during the retrial period has not been notarized or authenticated, and its authenticity cannot be confirmed. Even if the evidence were genuine, it could not prove that the bill of lading held by Xianfeng is authentic. (2) The bill of lading held by Meikuang has not been effectively endorsed continuously, and Odysseas Company's refusal to deliver the goods complies with legal provisions. The bill of lading held by Meikuang is a blank endorsed order bill of lading, and the carrier should transfer the bill of lading and deliver the goods according to the instructions of the shipper recorded on the bill of lading through endorsement. Therefore, the bill of lading must be effectively endorsed before delivery can be taken. Although the arbitral tribunal issued an award on the contract agreement between Meikuang and Mineral Company, the arbitral tribunal has already stated that its award only confirms the apparent right to take delivery. This case is a dispute over a contract of carriage of goods by sea, and the carrier should only deliver the goods to the lawful holder of the bill of lading.

During the retrial, Meikuang and Xianfeng submitted new evidence to this Court.

Meikuang submitted two pieces of evidence to this Court: 1. Notarial Certificate No. (2016) Hudong Zhengjing Zi 12417 and the signing receipt of the second instance court, intended to prove that the email regarding the delivery order submitted by Meikuang in the second instance was notarized, rather than being merely a printout of an email as recorded in the second instance judgment; 2. The service certificate of the second instance court and the parties' opinions on the evidence, intended to prove that Audacy Company and Xianfeng had expressed opinions on the Notarial Certificate. This Court, upon review, considers that the above evidence submitted by Meikuang had already been submitted during the second instance proceedings, and the second instance court had already conducted evidence examination and authentication on the above evidence. Therefore, the above evidence is not new evidence.

Xianfeng submitted new evidence to this Court: 1. Declaration of RADIANT Company, intended to prove that RADIANT chartered the vessel on behalf of Xianfeng; 2. Declaration of Sacvianam Company, intended to prove that Sacvianam Company purchased insurance on behalf of Xianfeng; 3. Cargo transportation insurance policy of the People's Insurance Company of China, intended to prove that the insured party for the Audacy vessel was Sacvianam Company; 4. Debit note from Minmetals Insurance Brokerage (Beijing) Co., Ltd., intended to prove that the company handled marine transportation insurance on behalf of Sacvianam Company; 5. Interview Record of Shanghai Maritime Court dated July 8, 2014, Trial Transcript of Case No. (2020) Humin Zhong 427, and the bill of lading submitted by Audacy Company in Case No. (2020) Humin Zhong 427, intended to prove that Audacy Company confirmed that RAINBOW Company was its agent, Mineral Company confirmed that it agreed to record Xianfeng as the shipper, and Audacy Company also admitted in Case No. (2020) Humin Zhong 427 that it had issued three sets of bills of lading, two of which listed the shipper as Xianfeng and one listed the shipper as Mineral Company.

Meikuang and Audacy Company argued in their opinions on the evidence that the Declaration of RADIANT Company and the Declaration of Sacvianam Company had not been notarized or authenticated, and their authenticity could not be confirmed. Even if they were genuine, since the two companies are affiliated with Xianfeng, they have an interest in the matter, and the declarations should not be accepted; Xianfeng's evidence items 3, 4, and 5 are not related to this case.

This Court believes that the Declaration of RADIANT Company submitted by Xianfeng has been notarized and authenticated, meeting the formal requirements stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Combined with the facts that RADIANT Company entered into a voyage charter party with Neptune Company for the transportation of the goods in question and that Xianfeng performed the relevant contracts, the relevant evidence can corroborate each other. Although Audacy Company and Meikuang raised objections to this evidence, they did not provide rebuttal evidence. This Court accepts the Declaration of RADIANT Company. Evidence item 5 corroborates other evidence and can prove that Mineral Company agreed to record Xianfeng as the shipper. Evidence item 2, the Declaration of Sacvianam Company, has not been notarized or authenticated, and evidence items 3 and 4 are not directly related to this case.

This Court confirms the facts found by the original trial court.

This Court further finds that on February 10, 2014, RADIANT Company, on behalf of Xianfeng, entered into a voyage charter party with Neptune Company and paid the freight on behalf of Xianfeng.

Additionally, the first and second instance courts have already found that on February 5, 2014, Mineral Company entered into a sales contract with SGL Company, and on February 6, 2014, Xianfeng entered into a sales contract with CBH Company. Both contracts concerned iron ore fines, with the country of origin being Iran, the producer being SABANOOR MINES, and the price being USD 59.75 per dry metric ton. The quantity was 50,000 wet metric tons, +10% at buyer's option. Regarding payment, Xianfeng paid a 50% down payment in accordance with the sales contract between it and CBH Company. SGL Company paid Mineral Company 50% of the total trade contract price on February 28 and March 12, 2014. Regarding the change in the shipper's record, there was a process where the shipper recorded on the mate's receipt, Mineral Company, was eventually changed to the shipper recorded on the bill of lading, Xianfeng, and this change was agreed to by Mineral Company. Based on the above facts and from the perspective of preponderance of evidence, it can be determined that the sales contract between Xianfeng and CBH Company and the sales contract between SGL Company and Mineral Company refer to the same goods. All the aforementioned contracts adopted the FOB trade term. Relatively speaking, Mineral Company was in the position of seller, and Xianfeng was in the position of buyer.

This Court believes that Neptune Company, its domicile, and the facts concerning the issuance of the disputed bill of lading are all located outside the territory of the People's Republic of China. According to Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-related Civil Relations (I), this case involves foreign-related elements. Article 8 of the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-related Civil Relations stipulates that the characterization of a foreign-related civil relationship shall be governed by the law of the forum. Xianfeng and Meikuang both requested Audacy Company and Neptune Company to deliver the goods based on their bills of lading. Audacy Company and Neptune Company raised corresponding defenses. Pursuant to the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, the first and second instance courts correctly characterized this case as a dispute over a contract of carriage of goods by sea. Regarding the applicable law, all parties unanimously chose to apply the law of the People's Republic of China during the first instance. According to Article 3 of the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-related Civil Relations, the first and second instance courts correctly applied the law of the People's Republic of China to hear this case.

Based on the retrial applications of Meikuang and Xianfeng, the disputed issues in this case are: 1. The identification of the legal status of the relevant parties; 2. Whether the claims of Xianfeng and Meikuang to take delivery of the goods based on their respective bills of lading should be upheld; 3. Whether Audacy Company and Neptune Company should bear related liability for damages.

I. Legal Status of the Relevant Parties

Regarding the legal relationship among Xianfeng, Audacy Company, and Neptune Company: The shipowner, Audacy Company, entered into a time charter party with Neptune Company, time-chartering the vessel to Neptune Company. The master and crew of the vessel "AUDACIOUS" were provided by the shipowner, Audacy Company. Audacy Company is the shipowner, and Neptune Company is the charterer. Neptune Company entered into a voyage charter party with RADIANT Company. Since the contract was signed by RADIANT Company on behalf of Xianfeng with Neptune Company, it can be determined that a voyage charter party relationship existed between Xianfeng and Neptune Company, with Neptune Company as the owner and Xianfeng as the charterer. In the time charter party between Audacy Company and Neptune Company, it was agreed that the shipowner authorized the charterer or its agent to issue bills of lading on behalf of the master or shipowner based on the mate's receipt. Based on the authorization given by the master of "AUDACIOUS" to RAINBOW Company on behalf of the vessel "AUDACIOUS," RAINBOW Company issued the bill of lading on behalf of the master of "AUDACIOUS." Pursuant to Article 72(2) of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, the bill of lading in question shall be deemed to have been issued by Audacy Company. Xianfeng is the shipper recorded on the bill of lading and holds the bill of lading in question. Since the bill of lading was issued by Audacy Company, not Neptune Company, it can be determined that a bill of lading carriage relationship existed between Xianfeng and Audacy Company.

Regarding the legal status of Meikuang: In this case, Meikuang intervened in the lawsuit as a third party with independent claims. Although it also holds a bill of lading, it obtained the bill of lading because Mineral Company used it to offset debts. The bill of lading in question is an order bill of lading. Mineral Company is neither the shipper recorded on the bill of lading nor did it obtain the bill of lading through endorsement transfer. It delivered the bill of lading to Meikuang by using it to offset debts. This type of delivery does not constitute an endorsement transfer under an order bill of lading. Meikuang is neither the shipper nor the holder of the bill of lading in the legal relationship of carriage of goods by sea.

II. Whether the Claims of Xianfeng and Meikuang to Take Delivery of the Goods Based on Their Respective Bills of Lading Should Be Upheld

(1) Whether the Bill of Lading Held by Xianfeng Is Forged

The first and second instance courts held that, first, the bill of lading in this case was issued by the signing agent RAINBOW Company on behalf of the master. As the actual issuer, its ability to identify the bills of lading it issued is significantly higher than that of other parties. RAINBOW Company confirmed that the bill of lading held by Mineral Company was genuine and that the bill of lading held by Xianfeng was forged. Second, the carrier controls the format and issuance of the bill of lading and is obligated to verify the authenticity of the bill of lading. Its identification of the bill of lading should also be one of the bases for determining its authenticity. Audacy Company and Neptune Company both agreed with RAINBOW Company's opinion that the bill of lading held by Xianfeng was forged. Although Xianfeng claimed that the bill of lading it held was obtained by an employee of RADIANT Company from RAINBOW Company, this statement was not confirmed by Audacy Company or Neptune Company, and Xianfeng did not submit further evidence to corroborate its statement. Therefore, Xianfeng cannot prove that the bill of lading it held was obtained through normal channels. Additionally, the actual payment made by Xianfeng had not yet reached the condition for the transfer of ownership of the goods as stipulated in the trade contract. Thus, the first and second instance courts determined that Xianfeng's bill of lading was forged.

This Court believes that, first, for Xianfeng, RAINBOW Company, Audacy Company, and Neptune Company are all interested parties in the bill of lading issuance process. In shipping practice, after the carrier or its agent receives or loads the goods, generally, one set of original bills of lading is issued at the shipper's request. However, due to mistakes or other reasons, the possibility of issuing more than one set of bills of lading for the same batch of goods received or loaded cannot be completely ruled out. Whether the bill of lading is correctly issued directly affects whether the parties involved in the issuance should bear corresponding responsibilities. Therefore, the parties involved in the bill of lading issuance, including the carrier, its master, or its agent, are all interested parties in the issuance of the bill of lading. In this case, although the signing agent RAINBOW Company stated that the bill of lading held by Xianfeng was forged, RAINBOW Company is an interested party in the bill of lading issuance process. Although Audacy Company and Neptune Company also agreed with RAINBOW Company's statement, they are also interested parties in the bill of lading issuance process. For the holder of the bill of lading claiming rights, the increase in the number of interested parties does not change the fact that they are still in the chain of interested parties.

Second, determining that Xianfeng is the lawful holder of the bill of lading in question would not completely violate the usual and reasonable practices of shipping operations, so Xianfeng's claim could be denied. However, such a situation does not exist in this case. The first and second instance courts held that, according to the terms of the trade contract, ownership of the goods would only transfer upon payment of 98% of the purchase price. However, Xianfeng had only paid 50% of the purchase price to its seller, CBH Company. This fact could be considered as a factor in denying the authenticity of the bill of lading held by Xianfeng. This Court believes that, in the special circumstance where two sets of original bills of lading exist for the same goods, considering whether the holder of the bill of lading has paid the agreed purchase price as a factor in assessing the reasonableness of the source and authenticity of the bill of lading is somewhat reasonable. However, when considering the facts related to the trade process, more attention should be paid to the relevant practices of bill of lading issuance under the relevant trade terms. Under a typical FOB trade term, the buyer or its agent is obligated to enter into a contract of carriage with the carrier. The buyer is the contractual shipper, and the seller is the actual shipper. Article 8(1) of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases of Disputes over Maritime Freight Forwarding does not deny the contractual shipper's right to obtain the bill of lading while stipulating that the actual shipper has the right to request the freight forwarding enterprise to deliver the bill of lading, sea waybill, or other transport documents. Therefore, it is not contrary to the usual practice of bill of lading issuance under a typical FOB term for the carrier to record the shipper on the bill of lading as the person who entered into the contract of carriage with it, including the buyer, the buyer's designated agent, or the person designated by the buyer's agent, and to deliver the bill of lading to that person.

Third, although RAINBOW Company, Audacy Company, and Neptune Company all recognized the authenticity of the bill of lading held by Meikuang, due to the interests of other parties claiming rights under the bill of lading, the authenticity of one party's bill of lading cannot be recognized and the authenticity of another party's bill of lading cannot be denied solely based on the statements of RAINBOW Company, Audacy Company, and Neptune Company, who are also interested parties, unless there is other corroborating evidence.

In summary, Mineral Company, Audacy Company, Neptune Company, and Meikuang did not provide conclusive evidence that Xianfeng forged the bill of lading. Xianfeng's holding of the bill of lading in question does not manifestly violate shipping practices. Based on the existing evidence and the rules for the allocation of the burden of proof, the conclusion of the first and second instance courts that the bill of lading held by Xianfeng was forged cannot be sustained.

(2) Whether the Claims of Xianfeng and Meikuang to Take Delivery of the Goods Based on Their Respective Bills of Lading Should Be Upheld

This Court notes that, in addition to the fact that the shipper on the bill of lading held by Xianfeng is recorded as Xianfeng, the shipper recorded on the bill of lading held by Meikuang is also Xianfeng. The legal consequences for the parties involved in the bill of lading are analyzed as follows:

For the Mineral Company: First, during the trial of first instance, the Mineral Company submitted a mate's receipt on which it was recorded as the shipper, and both Odysseus Company and Neptune Company acknowledged this evidence. The Mineral Company explained the fact that it was ultimately not recorded as the shipper on the bill of lading, while Pioneer Company was recorded as the shipper, stating that this was done to circumvent trade controls and meet the requirements of letter of credit settlement. In addition, the Mineral Company, Odysseus Company, and Neptune Company also submitted relevant email evidence intended to prove the negotiation process among the parties regarding how the bill of lading was to be issued, and further to prove that the bill of lading held by the Mineral Company was authentic and valid. This Court holds that the mate's receipt and the voided bill of lading recording the Mineral Company as the shipper could indeed prove the issuance process of the bill of lading, but the fact that the Mineral Company ultimately agreed to waive being recorded as the shipper on the bill of lading and agreed to have Pioneer Company recorded as the shipper means that the Mineral Company agreed to transfer to Pioneer Company, rather than the Mineral Company itself, the establishment of the corresponding transport relationship with the carrier. Second, because the bill of lading involved in this case is an order bill of lading, the transfer of the bill of lading cannot be accomplished without the endorsement of the shipper named on the bill of lading. By waiving being recorded as the shipper on the bill of lading, the Mineral Company, which had been recorded as the shipper on the mate's receipt, also relinquished the shipper's right to control the flow of the goods and secure payment for the goods through endorsement and transfer of the bill of lading. Third, although the Mineral Company still physically held one paper bill of lading, considering the evolution of the record of the shipper on the bill of lading and the final record of the shipper, the Mineral Company never held the status of shipper or holder of the bill of lading as defined by law.

With respect to Meikuang Company: Because the Mineral Company was neither the shipper named on the bill of lading nor did it obtain the bill of lading involved in this case through a complete chain of endorsements, there is a defect in the source from which the Mineral Company obtained the bill of lading. After the Mineral Company delivered the bill of lading to Meikuang Company, although Meikuang Company also physically held one paper bill of lading, similarly, Meikuang Company is not a holder of the bill of lading as defined by law. Since the source of the Mineral Company's bill of lading was already defective, and the Mineral Company delivered it to Meikuang Company by way of debt settlement with property, the rights obtained by Meikuang Company cannot be superior to those of the Mineral Company. Nor can the pre-existing defect be cured. Therefore, unless Pioneer Company, as the shipper named on the bill of lading and still holding the bill of lading, explicitly waives its rights under the bill of lading, the rights of Meikuang Company, whose source of the bill of lading is defective, will be subordinate to those of Pioneer Company based on its bill of lading.

In summary, based on the existing evidence, within the legal relationship of maritime cargo transport, Meikuang Company, in comparison, cannot rely on the bill of lading it possesses to oppose or exclude the bill of lading held by Pioneer Company. Pioneer Company is entitled to claim delivery of the goods from the carrier based on its bill of lading. Since the court of first instance sealed up the goods involved in this case on June 3, 2014, and auctioned the goods on December 23, 2014, and deposited the auction proceeds of RMB 6,821,281.95, Pioneer Company's claim that it is entitled to receive the auction proceeds of the goods involved in this case in the amount of RMB 6,821,281.95 has factual and legal basis and should be upheld. Meikuang Company's retrial request lacks factual and legal basis. The courts of first and second instance correctly held that the bill of lading held by Meikuang Company was not effectively and continuously endorsed and was transferred after the adoption of judicial preservation measures, and therefore Meikuang Company was not entitled to obtain the goods based on the bill of lading, and correctly denied Meikuang Company's demand for delivery. If Meikuang Company suffers losses due to its inability to retrieve the goods involved in this case, it may assert its rights based on other legal relationships, provided the statutory elements are satisfied.

III. Whether Odysseus Company and Neptune Company should bear relevant compensation liability.

Pioneer Company requested that Odysseus Company and Neptune Company be jointly and severally liable to compensate it for its cargo loss of RMB 17,251,124. However, during the proceedings of first and second instance, it submitted almost no substantive evidence regarding the amount of loss. First, during the first instance proceedings, it once submitted a Platts index report on international iron ore transaction prices, intending to prove the value of the goods involved at relevant time points, but later withdrew that evidence. During the retrial proceedings, it submitted a web printout of the Platts index annual average price of USD 96.7 per dry metric ton for 2014, and through the submission of its written submissions, stated the Platts prices for iron ore with 62% iron content at several time points. In its written submissions, it stated that the Platts price for the goods involved was USD 119.5 per dry metric ton on February 13, 2014, USD 68.25 per dry metric ton on December 17, 2014, and USD 71.75 per dry metric ton on December 31, 2014. By comparison, Pioneer Company's purchase price for the goods involved in early February 2014 was USD 59.75 per dry metric ton, and the auction price of the goods on December 23, 2014, was RMB 6,821,281.95. The goods involved are iron ore fines. Based on the evidence provided by Pioneer Company itself, the relationship between the contract price of its purchase of the goods and the Platts price for the goods during the same period, as well as the discrepancy between the auction price on December 23, 2014, and the Platts price during that period, Pioneer Company did not submit further evidence or provide a reasonable explanation for the causes of the discrepancy or its subsequent actual handling of the goods. Second, the goods arrived at the port of destination on April 12, 2014, and Pioneer Company claimed delivery on June 3, 2014. Pioneer Company claimed delivery only two months after the goods arrived. Even if there was a price difference loss, Pioneer Company did not submit relevant evidence or provide a reasonable explanation regarding whether such a price difference loss existed during those two months and how the responsible party should be determined. Therefore, Pioneer Company's claim that Neptune Company and Odysseus Company should compensate it for the price difference between its purchase price of the goods and the auction price of the goods is not supported by sufficient evidence. In conclusion, this Court does not uphold Pioneer Company's claim that Neptune Company and Odysseus Company should be jointly and severally liable for its loss of RMB 17,251,124. Correspondingly, because the factual basis for the loss base is insufficient, this Court also does not uphold Pioneer Company's claim for interest losses based on that base.

In conclusion, Pioneer Company's retrial requests are partially established and should be upheld. The judgments of first and second instance erred in fact-finding and application of law, and should be corrected. Pursuant to Paragraph 1 of Article 207 and Item 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders judgment as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2016) Hu Min Zhong No. 119 of the Shanghai High People's Court is reversed;

2. Item 1 of the main text of the civil judgment (2014) Hu Hai Fa Shang Chu Zi No. 838 of the Shanghai Maritime Court is reversed, and Item 2 of the main text of the civil judgment (2014) Hu Hai Fa Shang Chu Zi No. 838 of the Shanghai Maritime Court is affirmed;

3. The auction proceeds of the goods involved in this case, RMB 6,821,281.95, shall belong to Pioneer Export Company;

4. All other claims of Pioneer Export Company are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee for first instance: RMB 279,492, to be borne by Pioneer Export Company in the amount of RMB 116,211 and by Shanghai Meikuang Supply Chain Management Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 163,281. Court acceptance fee for second instance: RMB 279,492, to be borne by Pioneer Export Company in the amount of RMB 116,211 and by Shanghai Meikuang Supply Chain Management Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 163,281.

This judgment is final.
